video_title: The Ringer's Howard Beck on Caleb Wilson & NBA Offseason | By The Horns

quotes.speaker: K.C. Johnson
quotes.summary_phrase: Howard Beck admits he has not followed the Bulls recently
quotes.excerpt: he admitted that he has not really paid much attention to the Bulls in the past few seasons

text_blocks.speaker: K.C. Johnson
text_blocks.text: Full disclosure here, off the record, and I am violating rules here in sharing what he told me off the record. He admitted that he has not really paid much attention to the Bulls in the past few seasons. And really, for those national writers, you are not alone.

text_blocks.speaker: Howard Beck
text_blocks.text: The real disclaimer was more that I, during Summer League, was busy doing other things around Summer League and not watching Caleb Wilson or the other rookies.

quotes.speaker: Howard Beck
quotes.summary_phrase: Howard Beck on the difficulty of evaluating Summer League performances
quotes.excerpt: it is always hard to interpret the actual output because you are surrounded by mostly guys
quotes.quote: It is nice to watch the guys pop, especially the ones you really expect to. But we all know on this show here and everybody else in the NBA circles, you do not really know until you get into the season. And even then, it takes sometimes weeks, months, even years before you know for sure what you have. But very promising. And it is always hard to interpret the actual output because you are surrounded by mostly guys who are not going to be in the NBA. You are playing with teammates who you might have met five minutes ago and are not your actual Bulls teammates.

quotes.speaker: Howard Beck
quotes.summary_phrase: Howard Beck on the Bulls' decision to rebuild too late
quotes.excerpt: they decided to finally pseudo-tank a little too late and now they cannot prolong that
quotes.quote: The tough thing is they decided to finally pseudo-tank a little too late and now they cannot prolong that. Most teams you want to tank for a few years to get multiple bites at the apple at the top of a draft. They cannot do that because they just changed all the lottery odds. So now you almost have to win. I wonder if in a different version of events, if there is no lottery reform, are they still signing or still trading for Claxton and signing Norman Powell? Or are they leaning a little bit more into the overdue teardown to try to get more bites at the apple, more more high picks?

quotes.speaker: Cam Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Smith argues the Eastern Conference is now better than the West
quotes.excerpt: this is the first time in a while that the East in my opinion has been better

text_blocks.speaker: Cam Smith
text_blocks.text: Correct me if I am wrong, Howard, but for me, this is the first time in a while that the East in my opinion has been better than the Western Conference. When you look at how the teams stack up and where they are, I think the East is really, really difficult now.

text_blocks.speaker: Howard Beck
text_blocks.text: There is an argument to be made here about East versus West because at the very top, San Antonio and Oklahoma City are still so, so good. And that is no disrespect to the Knicks, the Sixers, the Cavs, the Pistons, the Celtics, anybody else. But the Thunder and the Spurs are just incredible.

quotes.speaker: Howard Beck
quotes.summary_phrase: Howard Beck on LeBron James' career-long focus on winning championships
quotes.excerpt: they are always informed by where can I win a championship
quotes.quote: They are always informed by where can I win a championship. And I guess, and I am guilty of this myself, as I said so in the piece, that I thought this time, because we are at the end, and because one of the themes of LeBron's career movements has been kind of like these separate chapters, right? Like he is almost like a storyteller in this regard. Going to Miami was, he framed it in reverse after the fact in his Sports Illustrated essay when he went back to Cleveland. He framed Miami as like, I never went to college, that was like college for me. I grew up there. I learned a lot. I figured out how to be a champion. I learned from Dwyane Wade and Pat Riley, or whoever he listed in that essay, but that was where I grew up and became a champion. Now I need to come home, kind of, you know, almost like to set things right. I want to bring a championship to Northeast Ohio, but I also want to be an inspiration for kids here where I grew up, especially for kids who grew up the way that he did.

quotes.speaker: Howard Beck
quotes.summary_phrase: Howard Beck on LeBron James' evolution into a primary playmaker
quotes.excerpt: he came into the league as quote more magic than Michael
quotes.quote: He came into the league as quote more magic than Michael. People laugh at that now and they say, what in the world are you talking about? At that size with those skills, of course he was going to be an all-time great scorer. But nobody ever thought he was going to get the all-time scoring record. In fact, 10 years ago, we were saying, was Kevin Durant going to be the one to threaten Kareem? And LeBron by that time had established himself as a pretty great scorer, but he was wired as a playmaker and a passer. That was his gift coming out of high school, and he was not a complete scorer yet. He did not have the three-point shot, he did not have the post game. That stuff came later. He still scored a lot anyway, just because he is as skilled and as smart and as physical as he is. But the guy can control the game in so many different ways with his playmaking, with his court vision.

quotes.speaker: Howard Beck
quotes.summary_phrase: Howard Beck clarifies that LeBron James has always been a point guard
quotes.excerpt: LeBron James has been the point guard on every fucking team he has ever been on
quotes.quote: Mario Chalmers was not the point guard of the Miami Heat, people. I am sorry. Mo Williams was not the point guard. They were playing off of him. He runs the damn show of every team that he is on, and he should. So, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, VJ Edgecombe, Anthony Simons, when he is coming into the game, Embiid of course, these guys are going to get KCP, they are going to get great shots because LeBron is going to make them more open than they have ever been. And even if he is not viewed as the same kind of threat that he once was, first of all, he will punish you the second you start to sag off of him anyway, but they are going to have to guard him.

quotes.speaker: Howard Beck
quotes.summary_phrase: Howard Beck on the inevitability of the Bucks' decline
quotes.excerpt: I think this was inevitable and a lot of us have been writing and talking about this
quotes.quote: I think this was inevitable and a lot of us have been writing and talking about this for years already because the Bucks were on such a clear downward trajectory. And yes, you know, Giannis's own health has had something to do with that, but it is just the erosion of the roster around him that has been happening ever since they won the championship. So in one sense, this is inevitable and maybe even overdue. But in another sense, it is still sad and it is still weird. And yeah, like we could, you know, everybody photoshops within seconds after these deals happen, but when we actually see him in the jersey for real in October, that is when it is going to, man, like that just, it is just bizarre. We will get used to it.

quotes.speaker: Howard Beck
quotes.summary_phrase: Howard Beck on the risks of the Clippers' investigation
quotes.excerpt: you could not let this get to July 1st
quotes.quote: It sucks that it has taken this long, but I just want to say benefit of the doubt to the league on this because I would be the first to say you could not let this get to July 1st. I was saying ever since this happened, I do not know when the results are coming or the conclusions are coming of this investigation, but the one thing I do know is it cannot leech into the off-season because you need to know the status of your players and who you need to acquire. And who, like if his contract is going to get voided and you are the Clippers, you need to know that before you get to July 1. And here we are in, you know, almost August and we still do not have a result. So I will be the first to say this has taken too long.

quotes.speaker: Howard Beck
quotes.summary_phrase: Howard Beck on the Clippers' interest in re-signing Bennedict Mathurin
quotes.excerpt: the Clippers do have interest in re-signing Bennedict Mathurin
quotes.quote: The original report comes from our our our guy Mark Stein, long-time national NBA guy who runs his own Substack now. Always plugged in, always accurate. So when he reported it, I I did some checking into it and here is I kind of frame what I have been told and what I know about the situation. The Bulls do indeed have interest, which again, I was never going to doubt Mark Stein because he is always accurate. But the most important thing to remember here is Bennedict Mathurin as we all know is a restricted free agent, right? So those are always tricky because you do not drive the bus. The Clippers are going to be involved in this process whether he comes to another team or whether he is resigned. And one thing I want to emphasize is that I was told is that the Clippers do have interest in re-signing Bennedict Mathurin. However, their big business is a little bit on hold right now as that Kawhi Leonard investigation that we talked about with Howard plays out.

quotes.speaker: Cam Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Cam Smith on Bennedict Mathurin's potential impact on the Bulls
quotes.excerpt: he is a guy that I have always respected about Ben Mathurin

text_blocks.speaker: Cam Smith
text_blocks.text: He is a guy that I have always respected about Ben Mathurin, and seeing how his game has developed in the NBA, especially with his shot and his offensive skill set. So, take us through what you have been hearing with Ben Mathurin and the latest in possibly being a Chicago Bull.

text_blocks.speaker: Howard Beck
text_blocks.text: One of the things I like about him is he plays hard, he plays through injury. He is kind of old school that way. He was injured last year and he played through injuries after that trade because he wanted to make a good impression on the Clippers. He is a great driver. He does sometimes tend to get in a little bit of isolation play, although he is excellent in transition. Not a great three-point shooter, although he shot well for the Clippers last year. So maybe some there might be some spacing issues, but he gets to the line a bunch. He is a hard driving player. He goes hard to the rim, whether it is in transition or in the half court.

quotes.speaker: Howard Beck
quotes.summary_phrase: Howard Beck on his conversation with Bennedict Mathurin
quotes.excerpt: the only conversation I have had with Bennedict Mathurin was in both of their shared rookie seasons
quotes.quote: The only conversation I have had with Bennedict Mathurin was in both of their shared rookie seasons. I went into the Pacers locker room before a road game in Indy, Bulls at Pacers, and Daylen Terry's name was kind of getting dragged through the mud a little bit. It was, you know, about midway through the season and I talked to Bennedict Mathurin and he talked up his teammate and said he is going to figure it out. And unfortunately, we had a great conversation, talked to him about 10 minutes. Really nice, respectful guy. Unfortunately, Daylen is looking for a job now because the one of the casualties of the LeBron James move was Daylen Terry getting waived, I believe, by Philadelphia.
